full_judgment:
6. Being aggrieved by the above order opposite party No. 1 Khan Ashraf Ali who came up third in the contest filed an appeal being Election Tribunal Appeal No. 4 of 1993 in the Court of the learned District Judge, Bagerhat on 7-3-1993 but Syed Matiur Rahman who came out in the 2nd position did not file any appeal and was quite content with the judgment. 

 7. Thereafter the appeal was transferred to the Court of the learned. Additional District Judge, Bagerhat for hearing and the learned Judge heard the appeal in part on 18-10-1994 and fixed the further hearing on 7-2-95 when he ordered to bring the ballot papers of all the election centres of the Tellegati Union Parishad to the Court to arrive at a rightful decision fixing next date on 7-3-1995 when the ballot papers were not brought the next date was fixed on 30-3-1995 but the ballot papers were not brought. 

 and in view of such circumstances there is no necessity of recounting of the ballot papers. The learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that there is no necessity of recounting, still the Appellate Court illegally ordered to bring all the ballot papers of the three wards for re-counting when the appellant's dispute is in one centre i.e. Telegati Centre. Mr. Latifur Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, submitted that the secrecy of ballot box would not be disturbed on mere prayer of a defeated candidate when he has failed to prove any of the allegations of malpractices against his opponents or the election officials. Mr. Latifur Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, has referred to 38 DLR (AD) 275 and has submitted that re-counting of ballot papers by the Tribunal is not specifically provided in the election rules and secrecy of the ballot papers should not be disturbed only because the defeated candidate wanted to re-count this. Mr. Latifur Rahman further referred to 28 DLR 375 and has submitted that sanctity of the ballot box should not be disturbed, only because the defeated candidate wanted to recount this. Mr. Latifur Rahman vehemently argued that ballot papers of three wards (three centres) were called for by the appellate Court when in both the election petitions prayer was for re-counting of only one centre i.e. centre No. 1 (Telegati Centre). Mr. Latifur Rahman further submitted that the signature of Ashraf Khan was taken in the result sheet of centre No. 1 and thereafter he cannot apply for re-counting of the ballot papers of centre No. 1 (i.e. Telegati Centre). 

 10. Mr. Sheikh Atiar Rahman with Mr. Abdur Rashid appearing for the opposite party has submitted that by the impugned order dated 7-2-95 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Bagerhat ballot papers of three centres were called for “অত্র আপীলে সঠিক সিদ্ধান্তে আসার জন্য” and the learned Additional District Judge committed no illegality in Milling for the ballot papers of the three wards for the purpose of disposal of the appeal and the learned Additional District Judge has not yet given any decision and, as such, the present petitioner cannot be called as an aggrieved person and he cannot come before this High Court Division to prefer revision against the order dated 7-2-95 which is only an interlocutory order. Mr. Sheikh Atiar Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party, has submitted that the revision lies only against a decision on merits by the appellate Court, not against the interlocutory order in calling for the ballot papers. Mr. Sheikh Atiar Rahman in support of this argument has referred to 39 DLR 140 and has submitted that the Election Tribunal as well as election appellate Tribunal is a court (to be treated as a civil Court) and has all the powers of the civil Court to call for the records of any election dispute. Mr. Sheikh Atiar Rahman further submitted that when the order is a final one regarding an election petition and the election petition is disposed of then the same would be appealable within the meaning of sub-section 4 of section 29 of the Union Parishad Ordinance, 1983. Mr. Sk. Atiar Rahman has submitted that the order for re-counting of ballot papers passed by the Election Tribunal or the election appellate Tribunal is not appealable. Mr. Sk. Atiar Rahman, appearing for the opposite party, has submitted that no illegality has been committed by the learned Additional District Judge in calling for the ballot papers when there are clear allegations of the opposite party (petitioner in the Election case No. 9 of 92) against the election officials in conducting the election and the learned Additional District Judge, Bagerhat has acted in his inherent power to do justice in the case and to arrive at a clear decision. Mr. Sk. Atiar Rahman has developed his argument by saying that the present petitioner has not yet been aggrieved as no decision has been given by the appellate Court and the Rule obtained by the present petitioner is liable to be discharged. 

 ”48. Power of the Tribunal The Tribunal shall have all the powers of a civil Court trying a suit under the Code of Civil Procedure (V of 1908), and shall be deemeto be a civil Court within the meaning of sections 480 and 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (V of 1898)." 

 From considering the above rules 47 and 48 of the Union Parishad Election Rules, 1983 I think the Election Tribunal would exercise all the powers of the civil Court treating the same under the Code of Civil Procedure, the appeal being the continuation of the suit/petition the appellate Court shall have all the powers of the civil Court, but the decision reported in 41 DLR 379 upon Upazila Parishad (Election of Chairman) Rules, 1983, their Lordships Mr. Justice Mohammad Ismail Uddin Sarker and Mr. Justice DM Ansar Uddin Ahmed came to the conclusion that, 

 "Although Rule 47 of the said Rules provides that the election petition shall be tried as nearly as may be in accordance with the procedure for the trial of suits under the Code of Civil Procedure and Rule 48 provides that the Tribunal shall have all the powers of a civil Court trying a suit under the Code of Civil Procedure and shall be deemed to be a civil Court within the meaning of sections 480 and 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, it is now well settled that the Election Tribunal is not Court constituted under the Civil Court Act In that view of the matter the power of an Election Tribunal trying an election petition under section 23 of Ordinance No. LIX of 1982 is that of a statutory tribunal with limited jurisdictions." 

 But in the present case, the court of appeal below has not yet given any judgment on merits after discussion of evidence, hence the decision reported in 41 DLR 379 may be distinguished. 

 13. It appears that in Election Tribunal Case No. 9 of 1992 corresponding to Election Tribunal Case No. 15 of 1992 in the prayer portion only the result of the center No. 1 was challenged and there was a prayer for declaring the election of the present petitioner as Chairman be declared illegal and in the Election Petition No. 12 of 1992 corresponding to Election Petition No. 18 of 1992 there was a prayer for declaration of the present petitioner as Chairman is illegal and in his place the petitioner in the Election Petition be declared as Chairman after re-counting of votes. It appears to me that the court of appeal below has not yet decided the appeal but by the impugned order dated 7-2-95 the learned court of appeal below has only called for the ballot papers of three wards of the Union Parishad to arrive at a correct finding in the appeal and I think the court of appeal below has acted exercising inherent power to arrive at a clear finding and to do justice there are clear allegations against the present petitioner and the election officials. The court of appeal below has not yet passed any judgment on merits after perusing the records and discussing the evidence on record and I think the Court of appeal below has committed no illegality in calling for the ballot papers of the three wards of No. 1 Telegati. Union Parishad by exercising the inherent power of the Court and I think that the inherent power of the Court is there to arrive at a correct finding and to do justice to the parties and for this. I rely upon the decision reported in 38 DLR (AD) 275 para 13. 

 Send down the Lower Court records at once.
